package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a large-scale, coordinated spam campaign designed to game the Tea protocol's reward system. Thousands of nearly identical, non-functional or minimally functional packages are published under random names, with artificially inflated dependency graphs, solely to increase 'teaRank' and farm cryptocurrency rewards. This behavior pollutes the open source ecosystem, increases the risk of supply chain attacks, and undermines trust in package repositories.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, the package.json declares thousands of dependencies on other spam packages from the same campaign, artificially inflating the dependency graph and teaRank score.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages rarely have thousands of dependencies, especially on other obscure or non-functional packages. This pattern is indicative of automated, coordinated spam.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies. Here, dependencies are used to manipulate ranking algorithms, not for technical necessity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Large meta-packages or frameworks may have many dependencies, but not in this random, interconnected, and non-functional manner.
key_indicators: Thousands of dependencies on similarly named, low-quality packages
No meaningful code or utility in the package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, a tea.yaml file is included to register the package with the Tea protocol, enabling it to participate in the reward system and receive TEA tokens.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of tea.yaml in thousands of low-quality, randomly named packages is a clear indicator of automated registration for reward farming.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate projects use tea.yaml to register real, valuable open source projects. Here, it is used to mass-register spam.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate open source projects using Tea protocol for compensation.
key_indicators: tea.yaml present in every spam package
Unique codeOwner addresses for each spam package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At publish-time, a minimal or meaningless README.md is included, providing no documentation or utility, only to fulfill repository requirements.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README.md files are expected to provide documentation. Here, they are empty or contain only the package name, indicating automated, non-genuine publication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages provide meaningful documentation. Spam packages do not.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Initial scaffolding of new projects may have minimal README, but not at this scale.
key_indicators: README.md with only the package name or random text
No actual documentation or usage instructions

attack_chain.leads_to: Artificial inflation of teaRank scores for all involved packages.

attack_chain.action: Packages are published to npm and linked to empty or minimal GitHub repositories, often with fake or automated accounts.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with thousands of dependencies, especially on other obscure or low-download packages
Presence of tea.yaml in non-functional or minimal packages
Mass publication of packages with random, hyphenated names or Latin portmanteaus
file_indicators: README.md with only package name or random text
network_indicators: High volume of npm publish events from the same IP or API key
Automated creation of GitHub repositories with minimal content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with unusually high numbers of dependencies, especially if dependencies are also low-quality or recently published. Flag packages containing tea.yaml when combined with minimal code and documentation. Detect mass publication patterns (e.g., many packages from the same user or with similar naming schemes). Correlate with automated GitHub account creation and repository population. Use heuristics to identify interconnected spam networks and artificially inflated dependency graphs.
